transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My thoughts won’t slow down, and it’s gotten to the point where I can’t focus enough to do my work safely. I'm a pipefitting apprentice, and being on the job site when my head is spinning like this is just getting too dangerous.
Do you experience excessive worry or fear about specific things, like making mistakes at work or something happening to you or others, when your thoughts are racing?

When my thoughts are racing, it's not really fear—it's more like a chaotic overload of ideas about blueprints, money, and inventions blasting through my head all at once. But when I crash into a down mood, that's when the heavy guilt hits, and I constantly replay my mistakes and worry that I'm putting everyone on the job site in danger.
Can you tell me more about these mood swings, specifically how often you experience the shift from racing thoughts to feeling down and guilty, and how long each of these episodes typically lasts?

I swing from feeling on top of the world with my brain buzzing to crashing into deep guilt, and this whole rollercoaster has been going on for about five months now. However, those heavy, drained down periods where I feel completely worthless have been hanging over me for about nine months overall.

Can you estimate how many days in a row you typically experience the racing thoughts and high energy versus the days you feel down and guilty, and do these episodes follow a regular pattern or are they more random?

I'm not really sure of the exact number of days each phase lasts, and there doesn't seem to be a set pattern. The heavy, down feelings have been dragging on for about nine months, but the unpredictable rollercoaster of highs and crashes has been going on for the last five months. It's really random, and sometimes I can even swing between both extremes in the very same afternoon.

Can you clarify if there are periods where you feel completely normal, without either the racing thoughts and high energy or the heavy guilt and down moods, and if so, how often these normal periods occur?

I don't really have periods where I feel completely normal anymore. For the last several months, it has just been a constant rollercoaster of swinging between the highs and the crashes, or feeling completely drained. There hasn't been any real break in between.

Can you describe the longest period you've experienced either the high energy and racing thoughts or the down and guilty mood without switching to the other extreme, to help me understand the severity and fluctuation of your symptoms?

The heavy, down, and guilty mood has definitely been the longest stretch, lasting for a solid nine months where I just haven't felt like myself or cared about my usual activities. In contrast, the high-energy rollercoaster and mood swings have been constantly fluctuating back and forth over the last five months since I started the Miami project.
Can you tell me more about the longest period you had the high-energy phase without switching to a down mood, to better understand the pattern of your mood swings?

I'm not really sure of the exact number of days or weeks that the high phases lasted on their own. It's just been a constant, messy rollercoaster of highs and crashes for the last five months, so it's hard to say how long a high lasted without a dip.

Can you try to estimate or recall if there was ever a period, even if brief, where you felt extremely high-energy and had racing thoughts without immediately crashing into a down mood, and if so, roughly how long did that period last?

Yes, I definitely had periods like that, especially during the last five months since starting the Miami project. Those high-energy, wired phases—where my mind was racing like a busted compressor and I was taking on endless tasks—would actually last for weeks at a time before I'd eventually crash.

Can you estimate the longest period you experienced the high-energy phase, with racing thoughts and taking on many tasks, without any significant down period, to help clarify the duration of your manic or hypomanic episodes?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of days or weeks that the longest high phase lasted continuously before I hit a crash. All I can say is that this entire back-and-forth rollercoaster has been happening for the last five months. It's just really hard to pin down a precise timeline for those high periods on their own.

Can you think back to any time during the last five months when you had a period of high energy and racing thoughts that lasted at least four consecutive days without switching to a down mood, and if so, did anything significant happen during or after those periods?

Yes, during the last five months, I definitely had stretches lasting weeks at a time where I felt constantly wired, staying up all night sketching and taking on double shifts without crashing. But it caused a lot of tension, and my foreman eventually gave me a formal warning because my erratic behavior was a safety hazard. It got so bad that I ultimately had to step back from my apprenticeship entirely.

Can you confirm whether these high-energy periods, lasting weeks at a time, were accompanied by a decreased need for sleep, increased self-esteem, or involvement in activities that might have had painful consequences, such as excessive spending or risky behaviors?

Yes, during those highs I'd lie awake with my brain buzzing and barely need sleep, and I honestly felt like I was the only one who truly understood the piping system, thinking I could redesign the whole Miami water setup. I also did some risky things, like snapping selfies on the scaffold at 2 a.m. and impulsively messaging people in the middle of the night about starting my own company.

Did you experience any significant impairment in social or occupational functioning, or require hospitalization, during those high-energy periods, which could help distinguish between mania and hypomania?

I wasn't hospitalized, but my work and social life have been completely disrupted. I had to step back from my apprenticeship because my foreman said I wasn't safe or reliable on site, and I've stopped showing up for my friends and the community center. The union coordinator actually had me pause my training and sent me to an employee assistance program for this urgent assessment because things were falling apart.
Did you experience any psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, during your high-energy periods, which could indicate a more severe manic episode?

No, I haven't experienced anything like hearing voices or seeing things. While I felt incredibly confident and had some really big ideas during those times, I don't think I had actual hallucinations or delusions.

Can you describe any significant changes in your behavior or actions during the high-energy periods that had negative consequences, such as financial problems, damaged relationships, or legal issues, to help me understand the severity of your symptoms?

During those highs, I'd go from feeling on top of the world to blowing up at my foreman and my boyfriend over tiny comments. This erratic behavior caused major tension with my coworkers and led to a formal warning from my foreman. It got so bad that I eventually had to step back from my apprenticeship because I just wasn't safe or reliable on site anymore.

Did you experience any periods where you felt extremely high-energy and had racing thoughts, but without significant impairment in social or occupational functioning, to help me distinguish between mania and hypomania?

While it initially looked like youthful enthusiasm, those high-energy periods absolutely interfered with my ability to function safely and reliably. They quickly led to safety issues on the job, a formal warning from my foreman, and forced me to step back from my apprenticeship entirely. I also ended up completely stopping showing up for my friends and the community center because I just couldn't handle it.

Can you clarify if there were any periods where you experienced high energy and racing thoughts without significant impairment in your daily life or work, which would help differentiate between mania and hypomania?

In the very beginning, people just thought it was youthful enthusiasm, but it quickly became erratic and unsafe. There really weren't any high periods that didn't cause major impairment, since it eventually led to a formal warning, safety issues, and me having to step back from my apprenticeship and social life entirely.
To confirm, you're saying that even in the early stages of these high-energy periods, they still caused significant problems at work and in your personal life, correct?

Yes, that's correct. Even though it started out looking like intense enthusiasm, it quickly led to major issues. I ended up getting a formal warning at work for safety and punctuality, and eventually had to step back from my apprenticeship and stop going to the community center because I couldn't keep up or be reliable.

Did any of your high-energy periods, characterized by racing thoughts and decreased need for sleep, last for at least seven consecutive days, or were they typically shorter, lasting around four consecutive days?

I'm not entirely sure about the exact number of days these high-energy periods lasted consecutively. I wasn't really keeping track of the calendar during those times when my mind was racing like that.

Can you think back and try to estimate if any of your high-energy periods, with racing thoughts and decreased need for sleep, lasted long enough to be considered a full week or more without switching to a down mood?

Yes, those high-energy periods definitely lasted for a week or more—often several weeks at a time. During those stretches, I felt constantly wired, barely slept, and kept chasing new projects before I'd finally crash into a down mood.

Can you confirm whether any single episode of high energy and racing thoughts, without a significant down period, lasted at least seven consecutive days, which would be crucial in distinguishing between the diagnoses we're considering?

Yes, I can definitely confirm that. During those high periods, I would go for weeks at a time—well over seven consecutive days—feeling completely wired, staying up late, and constantly working on projects without any down periods before I'd eventually crash.
